Prolonged periods of slow growth, significant inflationary pressures, volatility and disruption in financial markets, continued uncertainties and disruptions arising from the COVID-19 pandemic (including the emergence of new variants), and other adverse economic conditions could lead to lower demand for loans, higher credit losses, and lower fee income, among other effects.
changes.reasoning: The 2021 disclosures retain the general possibility that COVID-19 and adverse conditions may cause higher credit losses, but no longer identify the 2020 elevated-exposure industries, small-business concentration, or collateral-value impact. The specific sector-level and collateral-related risk is therefore materially less specific and softened rather than retained or absorbed.
changes.title: COVID-19 Elevated Credit Exposure

changes.year1_quote: If interest rates are reduced further in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, we expect that our net interest income will decline, perhaps significantly.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: As interest rates on earning assets decline, our cost of funds may not decline commensurately. Conversely, rising rates may result in our cost of funds increasing more than expected.
changes.reasoning: Year-2021 retains the general interest-rate sensitivity of net interest income, but it no longer presents the specific COVID-19-driven further rate-cut scenario or the expectation that net interest income could decline significantly. The disclosure becomes broader and less severe, so it is softened rather than retained or absorbed.
changes.title: COVID-19 Net Interest Income Pressure

changes.year1_quote: The success of these measures is unknown, and they may not be sufficient to fully mitigate the negative impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, some measures, such as a suspension of mortgage and other loan payments and foreclosures, may have a negative impact on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The COVID-19 pandemic created economic, financial, and social disruptions that have adversely affected, and are likely to continue to adversely affect, our business, financial condition, and results of operations, including the direct and indirect impact on our employees, customers, communities, counterparties, service providers, other market participants, and actions taken by governmental authorities and other third parties in response to the pandemic.
changes.reasoning: Year-2 retains a broad qualitative risk that governmental responses to COVID-19 may adversely affect the company, but it no longer specifically discloses the uncertainty about the sufficiency of government measures or the distinct risks from mortgage/loan-payment suspensions and foreclosures. The litigation and regulatory-scrutiny risk is addressed more generally in Candidate 5, but the Year-1 disclosure's specific COVID-19 linkage and government-measure examples are not fully preserved.
changes.title: COVID-19 Government Measures and Litigation

changes.year1_quote: The length of the pandemic and the efficacy of the extraordinary measures being put in place to address it are unknown.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic will negatively affect our businesses, financial condition, liquidity, and results of operations will depend on future developments that are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted.
changes.reasoning: Year-2021 retains the core economic risk that the COVID-19 pandemic may continue to adversely affect the business and financial results, while expressly preserving the uncertainty about its duration and future effects. The recession-specific risk is not stated as separately as in Year-2020, but the central pandemic-duration and adverse-impact disclosure remains materially present in Candidate 1.
changes.title: COVID-19 Duration and Recession Risk
